title: Membership of an Encoded Pair
statement: Let $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $V$ be a language of binary strings, and let $x,u$ be binary strings. The encoding of $(x,u)$ belongs to the paired verifier language exactly when $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$ and the concatenation $xu$ belongs to $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of binary strings
replaced:
Let $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$ and $V \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$, write
$\langle x, u\rangle$ for the self-delimiting pair encoding of binary strings $x$
and $u$ ($x$ with every bit doubled, then the separator $01$, then $u$), and let
$V^{\mathrm{pair}}_{C,c}$ be the set of strings that the aligned pair parser
decodes as a pair $(x, u)$ with $|u| = C(|x|+1)^c$ and $xu \in V$. Then for all
binary strings $x$ and $u$, $\langle x, u\rangle \in V^{\mathrm{pair}}_{C,c}$ if
and only if $|u| = C(|x|+1)^c$ and $xu \in V$.
